genZNote: Step one of nitrification: it eats ammonia for energy and hands off nitrite to Nitrobacter, keeping the whole nitrogen cycle (and your aquarium filter) running.

morphology.motility: Motile via one or two polar/subpolar flagella
morphology.notes: Chemolithoautotroph — obtains energy by oxidizing ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO2-) rather than from organic carbon.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, freshwater, wastewater treatment systems, and aquarium/aquaculture biofilters
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Central to the first step of nitrification in soils, water treatment plants, and aquarium filtration

culture.growthCharacteristics: Slow-growing obligate chemolithotroph; requires ammonia as sole energy source
culture.colonyMorphology: Rarely characterized by colony morphology; typically studied in liquid culture or biofilm

identificationClues: Obtains all its energy from oxidizing ammonia to nitrite — will not grow on standard organic media
First step of the two-step nitrification process, handing nitrite to Nitrobacter-type organisms for the second step
Essential to municipal wastewater treatment nitrogen removal and to establishing a 'cycled' aquarium filter
Not associated with human or animal disease

examFacts.importantTest: Obligate growth on ammonia as energy source; nitrite production
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Performs the first step of nitrification (ammonia → nitrite), essential to the global nitrogen cycle and wastewater treatment
